guarantees.claim: When reset is active (rst_ni low), reg_hash_process_flag is cleared to 0.
When not in reset and reg_hash_process_i is high, reg_hash_process_flag is set to 1.
When not in reset, reg_hash_process_i is low, and any of hmac_hash_done, reg_hash_start_i, or reg_hash_continue_i is high, reg_hash_process_flag is cleared to 0.
guarantees.cond: !rst_ni and !reg_hash_process_i and (hmac_hash_done or reg_hash_start_i or reg_hash_continue_i)

guarantees.claim: When none of the set or clear conditions are active and not in reset, reg_hash_process_flag retains its previous value.

assumptions.claim: The signals reg_hash_process_i and the clear signals (hmac_hash_done, reg_hash_start_i, reg_hash_continue_i) must be mutually exclusive in assertion; the design gives priority to set, so simultaneous assertion would prevent a clear.
assumptions.cond: when set and clear are both high
assumptions.risk: reg_hash_process_flag remains set when it should be cleared, potentially corrupting hash processing state.

uncertain_points.claim: The intended priority between setting (reg_hash_process_i) and clearing (done/start/continue) is not documented; the current implementation gives set precedence, which may be incorrect if these events can overlap.
uncertain_points.cond: reg_hash_process_i asserted along with any of hmac_hash_done, reg_hash_start_i, reg_hash_continue_i
uncertain_points.risk: Incorrect state machine progression could occur if the flag erroneously stays high, leading to functional failure.
